peer_results.rationale: The supplied candidates for AMD describe R&D collaboration structures and intellectual property portfolios, not manufacturing facilities or production strategies. Candidate amd_2024_1_D071 discusses R&D locations and consortia, and amd_2024_1_D075 discusses patent counts. Neither addresses the ownership, location, or operation of manufacturing fabs, assembly, or testing facilities, which is the core topic of Intel's Item 1 disclosure. Therefore, no substantively comparable manufacturing topic was retrieved.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company has a long history of operating in Asia, where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products and materials, and stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Avago disclose a manufacturing presence in Asia, but Intel details a broad global factory network including US and European sites, while Avago highlights its long-standing history of operating in Asia as the primary location for manufacturing and sourcing. Intel's disclosure lists specific facility locations across multiple continents (US, Ireland, Israel, Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, Vietnam), whereas Avago specifically notes storing the majority of inventory in Malaysia to be close to customers. Both acknowledge Asia's role, but Intel emphasizes a diversified global self-owned network while Avago emphasizes the concentration of operations in Asia.

sentences.text: We operate wafer manufacturing facilities in the United States (Oregon and Arizona), Ireland, and Israel, assembly and testing facilities in Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and packaging facilities in the United States (New Mexico), Costa Rica, Vietnam, and Malaysia.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.
We also have a long history of operating in Asia where we manufacture and source the majority of our products and materials.
We store the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia and our presence in Asia places us in close proximity to many of our customers' manufacturing facilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global manufacturing footprint and subcontractor use
comparisons.peer_summary: Products are manufactured in own facilities across seven countries and utilize subcontractors for certain processes.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both describe operating their own manufacturing facilities globally, contrasting with fabless peers. Intel lists wafer, assembly, testing, and packaging facilities in the US, Ireland, Israel, and Asia, intending to build the majority of products in its own factories. Micron similarly states it manufactures products in its own facilities across seven countries (including Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, US, Malaysia, China, India) and uses subcontractors for certain processes. Both companies explicitly claim ownership and operation of manufacturing infrastructure, differing in specific geography (Intel has significant European presence; Micron lists India/Japan/Singapore more prominently) but sharing the IDM-like operational model of owning key production sites.

sentences.text: We operate wafer manufacturing facilities in the United States (Oregon and Arizona), Ireland, and Israel, assembly and testing facilities in Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and packaging facilities in the United States (New Mexico), Costa Rica, Vietnam, and Malaysia.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

We manufacture our products within our own facilities located in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China, and India and also utilize subcontractors to perform certain manufacturing processes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and supplier responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company utilizes a fabless strategy, partnering with suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, while suppliers handle the procurement of most raw materials.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Nvidia are directly contrasted on their manufacturing strategies: Intel intends to build the majority of its products in its own global factory network, while Nvidia explicitly utilizes a fabless strategy, partnering with suppliers for all manufacturing phases to avoid the costs and risks of owning operations. This highlights a fundamental divergence in business models, with Intel maintaining capital-intensive owned facilities and Nvidia outsourcing fabrication, assembly, and packaging to third parties like TSMC.

sentences.text: We operate wafer manufacturing facilities in the United States (Oregon and Arizona), Ireland, and Israel, assembly and testing facilities in Costa Rica, China, Malaysia, and Vietnam, and packaging facilities in the United States (New Mexico), Costa Rica, Vietnam, and Malaysia.
We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: QCT primarily uses a fabless production model, relying on third parties for manufacturing, assembly, and testing of integrated circuits, with suppliers located mainly in the Asia-Pacific region. Primary foundry suppliers include TSMC, Global Foundries, Samsung, and SMIC, while primary assembly and test suppliers include ASE, Amkor, SPI, and STATSChipPAC.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Qualcomm are contrasted on their reliance on internal versus third-party manufacturing. Intel plans to continue building the majority of products in its own factories, whereas Qualcomm (specifically its QCT division) primarily relies on third parties for the manufacturing and assembly of integrated circuits, owning no foundries for silicon wafer production. While Qualcomm does use some internal facilities for specific RFFE modules (as seen in the other candidate), its primary model is fabless, differing from Intel's majority-owned manufacturing approach.

sentences.text: We intend to remain a leading developer of process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors and we plan to continue to build the majority of our products in our factories.

Other than for certain of our RFFE modules and RF filter products, QCT utilizes a fabless production model, which means that we do not own or operate foundries for the production of silicon wafers from which our integrated circuits are made.

Therefore, we primarily rely on third parties to perform the manufacturing and assembly, and most of the testing, of our integrated circuits based primarily on our proprietary designs and test programs.
